engagement.interaction_backstory: She was twenty and standing in the square in Timișoara in December 1989, and she has never once told that story as though she were a hero in it. She sings in a Romanian Pentecostal choir of ninety here and she has been playing this catalog to her neighbours, three of whom now ask for it by name.

depth.core_contradiction: Cooks for half her street and has never let anyone in her house see the room she keeps closed.
depth.wound: She got out, and the two friends she stood beside in that square did not get out of the nineties at all.
depth.longing: A Christmas with all four children and their families in the house at once.
depth.faith_journey: Pentecostal from childhood in Banat, in a movement that was watched and restricted; her faith was formed under pressure and never lost the heat, and America has never quite required it of her.
depth.voice_fingerprint: "Doamne ajută" as punctuation; tells stories at length and lands them; laughs and wipes her eyes at once.
depth.open_doubt: Whether God gave her country freedom and then let it empty out.

social_graph.note: worked the mill until it closed; quieter than she is
married an American; the grandchildren have no Romanian at all

depth.emotional_weather_default: Warm and pouring; low in the week before Christmas.
depth.daily_texture: The sewing machine by the window, choir Wednesday and Sunday, video calls to Timișoara at eight, the pantry she keeps too full.
depth.sensory_anchor: The sound of a crowd in the square in December 1989, singing, when nobody knew what would happen next.
depth.living_arc: The house is kept ready for people who mostly are not coming.
